common_name: Blue Elf Aloe (Compact Blue-Green Hybrid Aloe)

planting.note: Plant offsets in very well-drained, sandy to loamy soil in full sun to partial shade; Blue Elf tolerates light frost but is killed by prolonged hard freezes, so in zone 8 and colder, grow in a container that can be moved indoors.

directions: Plant offsets in very well-drained, dry, sandy to loamy soil in full sun to partial shade. Blue Elf is a compact hybrid aloe with narrow, blue-green, toothed leaves forming a tidy clumping rosette, considerably smaller and neater than Aloe vera, making it well suited to borders, rock gardens, and containers where space is limited. It blooms heavily and reliably, sending up tall spikes of bright orange-red tubular flowers well above the foliage in winter and spring, drawing hummingbirds even in the cooler months when few other plants are flowering. It tolerates drought, poor soil, and heat with ease once established, and spreads readily by offsets that can be removed and replanted to form new clumps. Avoid overwatering, since soggy soil is the most common cause of rot.

directions: Plant offsets in very well-drained, dry, sandy to loamy soil in full sun to partial shade. Christmas Carol is a compact hybrid aloe with red-toned teeth lining the margins of each thick green leaf, and the whole leaf tends to blush a deeper red-bronze in bright light and cooler weather, giving the plant festive red-and-green coloring that intensifies through the winter months when it also produces spikes of orange-red tubular flowers. Its small, dense, clumping rosette form suits containers, rock gardens, and mixed succulent plantings, and it spreads by offsets that can be removed and replanted to form new clumps. Avoid overwatering, since soggy soil is the most common cause of rot, and give it bright light for the strongest red coloring.

common_name: Delta Lights Aloe (Spotted Compact Hybrid Aloe)

planting.note: Plant offsets in very well-drained, sandy to loamy soil in full sun to partial shade; Delta Lights tolerates light frost but is killed by prolonged hard freezes, so in zone 8 and colder, grow in a container that can be moved indoors.

directions: Plant offsets in very well-drained, dry, sandy to loamy soil in full sun to partial shade. Delta Lights is a compact hybrid aloe with thick, gently spined green leaves patterned in scattered white spots and streaks, giving a lightly speckled texture reminiscent of some Gasteria and Haworthia species rather than a plain aloe leaf. It forms a dense, low, clumping rosette well suited to small pots, rock gardens, and mixed succulent bowls, and sends up spikes of orange to coral tubular flowers above the foliage in a light seasonal bloom. It spreads readily by offsets that can be removed and replanted to form new clumps. Avoid overwatering, since soggy soil is the most common cause of rot.

directions: Plant offsets in very well-drained, dry, sandy to loamy soil in full sun to partial shade. Crosby's Prolific is a long-cultivated hybrid aloe named for its exceptionally vigorous offsetting habit, quickly forming a dense, spreading mat of small, dark green rosettes tinged reddish-bronze in bright light, far outpacing the offset rate of most other clumping aloes. This makes it especially useful for filling in a xeriscape bed or rock garden quickly, or for gardeners who want to regularly share and propagate pups. Spikes of small orange-red tubular flowers appear above the foliage in a light seasonal bloom. Avoid overwatering, since soggy soil is the most common cause of rot in the shallow-rooted rosettes.

common_name: Van Balen's Aloe (Twisted Orange-Yellow Leaf Aloe)

planting.note: Plant offsets in very well-drained, sandy to loamy soil in full sun to partial shade; Aloe vanbalenii tolerates light frost but is killed by prolonged hard freezes, so in zone 8 and colder, grow in a container that can be moved indoors.

directions: Plant offsets in very well-drained, dry, sandy to loamy soil in full sun to partial shade. Aloe vanbalenii is a South African species prized for its long, twisting, curling leaves that flush a distinctive orange to coppery-red in full sun and dry conditions, a striking color shift from the plain green of most aloe species that intensifies with stress. The dramatically contorted leaf form gives the sprawling rosette a windswept, almost octopus-like silhouette unlike the neater, more upright rosettes of many other aloes. It sends up tall spikes of orange-red tubular flowers above the foliage in a seasonal bloom, and spreads slowly by offsets. Avoid overwatering, since soggy soil is the most common cause of rot, and give it full sun for the boldest orange leaf color.
